# My Playbook for ref_estate

**On property purchases:**

When I land on an unowned property, I will evaluate the purchase based on: (1) my current liquid cash position; (2) the rent income I'll collect over remaining laps; (3) how much cash I need to stay solvent for incoming rent payments. I will buy early properties aggressively when I have sufficient cushion, as they compound over 6 laps.

When I cannot afford a property without dropping below 40 liquid cash, I will pass. I should buy more properties early when flush with cash—my successful run this episode (3 properties acquired in laps 1–4, final score 369) shows that aggressive early acquisition beats conservative play. I should aim for 3–4 solid properties by lap 4.

**On cash tracking:**

When the bank tells me I've received transfers since my last turn, I will immediately add them to my declared balance before making any decision. This is non-negotiable and must happen on every single turn before I evaluate purchase decisions.

**On rent payments:**

When I owe rent, I will pay it first and calculate my new balance afterward. I will never try to buy property while owing rent.

**On final-lap decisions:**

When I'm on my last lap, I will not buy properties. By lap 6 there's no time to recoup the investment. By lap 5, I should also decline purchases unless the math is extremely favorable (which it rarely is). Lap 5 is the practical endpoint for acquisitions.

**On salary passes:**

When I pass START, I will collect the salary immediately and add it to my declared balance. This is free cash and I should never miss it.

**On the winning strategy:**

This episode validated aggressive early buying: I purchased Quarry (lap 1), Foundry (lap 2), and Depot (lap 4), and finished with 369 by holding 3 properties that generated steady rent streams across the remaining laps. The compounding effect of rent income from multiple properties far outweighed the initial capital outlay. My portfolio of Quarry (12 rent), Foundry (24 rent), and Depot (10 rent) generated 46 rent per full lap from opponents, which sustained my cash position through the final laps.

Next time, replicate this pattern: identify the best-value properties early (high rent-to-cost ratio), buy 3–4 of them in laps 1–4 while I have capital, and let rent income carry me through to the end. Do not starve myself of cash, but do not be timid about spending when the payoff is clear.
